canonical_topic: Common hedge structures: futures and costless collars
definition: Although almost any derivative can be used to hedge, futures/forwards/swaps and costless collars are the two most commonly used structures in practice.
core_idea: Futures, forwards, and commodity swaps are favored as hedging tools primarily because they can be entered into for free or for only a limited margin requirement, making them capital-efficient relative to other instruments.
key_points: A variety of futures, forwards, and commodity swaps can serve as hedging instruments
Futures-type hedges are attractive because they typically require little or no up-front premium, only margin
Costless collars are cited as the other most common hedge structure, for the same low-capital-requirement reason
trading_implications: Futures/forwards and costless collars are preferred hedge structures when a firm wants to minimize up-front cash outlay for the hedge
